title: Affect-Effect Primitive and Quantitative Projection Bridge
purpose: Define the qualitative RT primitive (A|E) and induct a quantitative bridge into overlap, probability, and statistical interpretation without identifying A and E as quantum states by default.

qualitative_primitive.name: affect-effect relational gradient
qualitative_primitive.meaning: (A|E) denotes the irreducible relational condition in which Affect and Effect are distinguishable but not independently defined outside their relation.
component_boundary: A is not an isolated object.
E is not an isolated object.
A and E acquire operational identity only within bounded evaluation.

quantitative_bridge.compression_warning: The compressed form suppresses M_R and must not be read as claiming raw RT conditions are automatically Hilbert-space vectors.
quantitative_bridge.probability_boundary: Probability is allowed only after normalization, event-space declaration, and measurement semantics are supplied.

M_R.name: reference-relative representation map
M_R.domain: C_RT, the set of admissible RT relational conditions
M_R.codomain: V_R, a declared quantitative representation space

governance_constraints: Do not describe |<A|E>|^2 as probability unless a normalized outcome set has been defined.
Do not identify A and E with quantum states unless a Hilbert-space interpretation is explicitly declared.
Do not collapse the qualitative primitive (A|E) into its quantitative projection.
Preserve reference, boundary, and orientation metadata when comparing projected values.
High overlap denotes projected compatibility, not identity, causation, or temporal succession.
open_questions: Should M_R be linear, nonlinear, or domain-selected?
Does distinction density determine the basis, weighting coefficients, or normalization of M_R?
Should Affect and Effect occupy the same representation space or dual spaces?
Is directional asymmetry preserved by a second phase or orientation term lost under squared magnitude?
Should the full RT bridge retain complex or signed amplitude before squaring?
Can non-Markov history be encoded directly into A, or must it remain an explicit additional argument H_t?
promotion_boundary: No canonical lexicon promotion beyond provisional L0/L1 without validation.
No physics claim that this derives quantum probability.
No claim that raw A and E are Hilbert-space states.

recommended_next_derivation.candidate: Define directional relational amplitude K_R(A -> E) before constructing the bounded projection.
